en_alt: Without reinforcements the city would have fallen.
note: Perfective бы+past also reads as a past counterfactual, so the 'would have' rendering is equally valid here.

ru: Без цвето́в в ко́мнате не па́хло бы так прия́тно.
en_alt: Without flowers it would not smell so pleasant in the room.
note: The Russian is impersonal (в ко́мнате па́хло), so the 'it … in the room' version tracks the structure and is equally good English.

ru: Ско́ро в до́ме бу́дет па́хнуть ёлкой.
Я передава́ла бы приве́т ка́ждый раз.
note: Habitual 'would pass on' is the correct imperfective reading; the collision is fixed on the perfective side (Я переда́л бы…).

en_alt: They were passing the news on to one another.

note: Imperfective past also supports the progressive reading, and 'pass on' matches the headword gloss.
Frame collision only: the partner is a perfective imperative about salt, so the sentence still cues its verb clearly.

ru: Тепе́рь я бу́ду передава́ть тебе́ но́вости.
en: Now I will be passing on the news to you.
note: Compound future of the imperfective is ongoing/repeated, so 'will be passing on'; this also clears both collisions with переда́м/переда́шь.

en_alt: He is passing the letter to the neighbour.
note: Present imperfective covers both the habitual and the progressive reading; the ты-sibling is already rendered progressively.

en_alt: Soon the courier will pass on the documents.
note: 'hand over' is fine, but the gloss-matching 'pass on' should also be accepted by the word-bank drill.
Correct as a single completed future event; the collision is fixed on the imperfective side.
Correct as a single completed future event; the collision is fixed on the imperfective side.

ru: Я переда́л бы ему́ твои́ слова́.
en: I would have passed on your words to him.
note: Perfective бы+past is a single completed event, so 'would have passed on'; this leaves the habitual 'would pass on' to the imperfective partner.

ru: Отны́не я бу́ду пережива́ть за тебя́ на экза́мене.
note: 'will worry' reads better than 'will be worrying' here and no collision is reported.

ru: Ты бы не пережива́ла и́з-за пустяко́в.

note: пережива́ть за + acc means 'to worry about'; the headword gloss 'to experience' does not cover this sense, which four of the six examples use — the gloss is likely the half that needs widening.
Sentence-final ско́ро is marked word order but not wrong.

en_alt: I would have got through this more calmly.
note: Perfective бы+past also carries the past-counterfactual reading.
перейти́ на / к here means 'move over, switch, transfer', a sense the headword gloss 'to cross' does not cover; three of the six examples use it.

ru: Я перешла́ бы доро́гу по перехо́ду.
en: I would have crossed the road at the crossing.
note: Perfective бы+past reads as a single completed event; this leaves the habitual 'would cross' to the imperfective partner (переходи́ла бы … то́лько на зелёный).
Correct for a single completed crossing; the collision is fixed on the imperfective compound-future side.
Correct for a single completed crossing; the collision is fixed on the imperfective compound-future side.
перенести́ боле́знь is 'to endure/come through an illness', and перенести́ встре́чу is 'to postpone'; neither sense is covered by the gloss 'to carry across'.

en_alt: They postponed the meeting until Friday.
note: 'postponed' is the usual English for перенести́ встре́чу and should be accepted too.

ru: Ты бы перенёс встре́чу на у́тро.
en_alt: You would have moved the meeting to the morning.
note: Perfective бы+past also carries the past-counterfactual reading.

ru: Я перенесу́ стол в другу́ю ко́мнату.
en_alt: I will carry the table into another room.
note: в + accusative is 'into'; both prepositions are natural here.

ru: Мы перенесём ме́бель в зал ско́ро.
note: Sentence-final ско́ро is marked word order but not wrong.

ru: Е́сли бы бы́ло вре́мя, я переоде́лась бы.
note: Perfective бы already rendered as 'would have changed' — correct.

en_alt: She changed for dinner.
note: English 'change' alone already implies clothes; both renderings are natural.

en_alt: Will you change for dinner?
note: English 'change' alone already implies clothes; both renderings are natural.

en_alt: We are moving on to the main question.
note: Present imperfective supports the progressive reading, which is what an English speaker would usually say in a meeting.

ru: С э́того дня я бу́ду переходи́ть у́лицу осторо́жно.
en: From this day on I will be crossing the street carefully.
note: Compound future of the imperfective is ongoing/repeated, so 'will be crossing'; this clears both collisions with перейду́ / перейдёшь.

ru: Я переходи́ла бы доро́гу то́лько на зелёный.
note: Habitual 'would cross' is the correct imperfective reading; the collision is fixed on the perfective side.

ru: Е́сли б знал слова́, я пел бы гро́мче.

ru: Весь день она́ бу́дет писа́ть отчёт.

Frame collision only; 'more water' vs the partner's partitive 'some water' still distinguishes the two imperatives.

en: In the morning I will be drinking tea.

ru: Ле́том я бу́ду пла́вать ка́ждый день.

ru: Я пла́ваю в бассе́йне ка́ждый день.

ru: Ты бы пла́вала лу́чше с трене́ром.

en_alt: They cried with happiness.
